case: restarted, and stage7 started 77 minutes later (incident 02): the restart is seen
output: NEXT: AfterRestart

case: not restarted, however long Windows has been running: asks for the restart
output: 2. Start > Power > Restart. |   3. Sign in again, wait one minute, then open this disc and double-click stage7 again.

case: not restarted, but the running time looks shorter (a clock jump): still asks for the restart
output: 2. Start > Power > Restart. |   3. Sign in again, wait one minute, then open this disc and double-click stage7 again.

case: no count of starts, the System log has a newer start: the restart is seen
output: NEXT: AfterRestart

case: count unchanged but the System log has a newer start: the restart is seen
output: NEXT: AfterRestart

case: neither count nor log, shorter running time: the restart is seen (the rule of versions 1 and 2)
output: NEXT: AfterRestart

case: neither count nor log, longer running time: asks for the restart and says within how many minutes
output: 3. Sign in again, wait one minute, then open this disc and double-click stage7 again. |   (This Windows keeps no count of its starts, so the check goes by running time: start stage7 within 38 minutes of the restart.)

case: no record of the install step's start of Windows: stops, the restarted phase is not run unchecked
output: STOPPED: the record of the Windows start the install step ran in (stage7-install-boot.json) is missing or cannot be read, so the restart cannot be checked. | Photograph this window for Claude and wait.

case: nothing to compare at all: stops
output: STOPPED: Windows offers nothing here that tells one start from the next, so the restart cannot be checked. | Photograph this window for Claude and wait.

case: real: the record is of this very start of this PC: asks for the restart
output: 2. Start > Power > Restart. |   3. Sign in again, wait one minute, then open this disc and double-click stage7 again.

case: real: the record is of an earlier start of this PC: the restart is seen
